---
title: Getting started with SearcherKit
---

SearcherKit is a modular runtime for building, running, evaluating, and
training search agents. It connects a language model to retrieval sources and
model-visible tools, while keeping agent logic, provider APIs, parsing,
execution, and observability as separate components.

Use this page to install SearcherKit and run your first local-file search. You
can then follow a task guide or explore the system concepts in more detail.

## How SearcherKit works

```text
dataset or TUI
      |
      v
 AgentRunner ---- checkpoint, logs, per-task retry
      |
      v
 SearchAgent ---- turn, token, and time budgets
      |
      +---- Parser <----> LLM Client <----> model endpoint
      |
      +---- Tool ----> Source ----> file, web, or Elasticsearch
      |
      `---- Tool ----> MCP server
```

At the center of this flow are three modules with different responsibilities:

- **Sources** connect SearcherKit to information. A source knows how to search
  and fetch documents from one backend, such as a local directory, the web, or
  an Elasticsearch index. It returns the same provider-neutral document types
  regardless of the backend.
- **Tools** turn capabilities into actions the model can call. A tool defines
  the model-visible name, description, and input schema, then delegates the
  work to one or more sources (or to an external service such as MCP). This
  keeps storage details out of the model's interface.
- **The LLM** drives the reasoning loop. The LLM client sends requests to the
  model endpoint, while the parser translates messages and tool calls between
  the model's format and SearcherKit's internal format. The model decides
  whether to call a tool, inspect its result, continue searching, or return a
  final answer.

A typical turn therefore forms a loop:

```text
question -> LLM -> tool call -> Tool -> Source -> documents
              ^                                  |
              `----------- tool result <---------'
```

Configuration defines how these modules are assembled. Under `agent`, each
source is declared with a `type`, a unique `name`, and backend-specific
settings. Each source-backed tool refers to one or more of those names, which
explicitly defines where the tool retrieves information. The `llm_client` and
`parser` entries select the model endpoint and the message/tool-call format
used to communicate with it.

At startup, SearcherKit composes the YAML configuration and uses factories to
construct the configured LLM client, parser, sources, and tools. It then gives
the tool definitions to the LLM and keeps the instantiated sources behind the
tools. In other words, config is not just a list of settings: it is the wiring
that determines which model can call which tools, which sources those tools can
reach, and which limits govern the agent loop. The same wiring is used whether
the run starts from the TUI or a dataset.

## Install SearcherKit

Clone the repository and install the package in editable mode:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ml-stat-Sustech/searcherkit.git
cd searcherkit
pip install -e .
```

Confirm that the command is available:

```bash
searcherkit --help
```

Local-file search uses [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) for
full-text matching. Install it separately and verify that `rg` is on `PATH`:

```bash
rg --version
```

The default installation includes the Elasticsearch and Anthropic clients.
Some deployment and training workflows require additional services or optional
dependencies; their task guides list the relevant requirements.

## Run your first search

The packaged `file_search` configuration connects an OpenAI-compatible model
endpoint to `search` and `visit` tools over a local directory.

Set the model endpoint and the directory to search:

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Bash

```bash
export LLM_MODEL="YOUR_MODEL"
export LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
export LLM_BASE_URL="https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
export FILE_SEARCH_ROOT="./docs"
```

### PowerShell

```powershell
$env:LLM_MODEL = "YOUR_MODEL"
$env:LLM_API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"
$env:LLM_BASE_URL = "https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
$env:FILE_SEARCH_ROOT = ".\docs"
```
:::

Start the interactive terminal UI:

```bash
searcherkit tui --config-name file_search
```

The agent can now search files under `FILE_SEARCH_ROOT`, open relevant results,
and use their contents to answer your questions.

See [Search files with SearcherKit](01-searching/01-search-files.qmd) for the
complete workflow, output locations, and access restrictions.

## Understand the configuration

A SearcherKit run is described by YAML. The smallest useful configuration
connects four parts:

- an LLM client that communicates with the model endpoint;
- a parser that converts messages and tool calls;
- one or more sources that retrieve documents;
- tools that expose selected source operations to the model.

```{.yaml filename="config.yaml"}
agent:
  llm_client:
    type: openai
    model: ${oc.env:LLM_MODEL}
    api_key: ${oc.env:LLM_API_KEY,EMPTY}
    base_url: ${oc.env:LLM_BASE_URL}
  parser:
    type: upstream
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: project_docs
      root_path: ./docs
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      source: [project_docs]
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [project_docs]
  system_prompt: >-
    Search for evidence when needed and give a concise final answer.
  max_turn: 10

output_path: outputs/first-run
```

Here, both tools refer to the source by its unique name, `project_docs`. The
`upstream` parser expects the provider to return structured tool calls. Models
that encode tool calls in text may require a model-specific parser.

If this file is saved as `configs/demo/config.yaml`, validate and run it with:

```bash
searcherkit inspect --config-path configs/demo --config-name config
searcherkit tui --config-path configs/demo --config-name config
```

Hydra-style overrides let you change values without editing the file:

```bash
searcherkit tui --config-path configs/demo --config-name config \
  agent.llm_client.model=Qwen3-8B \
  output_path=outputs/qwen3
```

Read [LLM integration](03-customizing/02-LLM-integration.qmd) for clients and
parsers, and [Sources and tools](03-customizing/03-sources-and-tools.qmd) for
retrieval and model-visible tool schemas.
